record: the paired static-vs-band refinement test - WITHDRAWN before approval; never executed
status: WITHDRAWN. Never approved, never dispatched, no Palace solve and no QMHP static solve was run for it. predeclaration.json is kept unchanged as the historical preparation; the dispatch workflow and the approval draft were removed (they remain in git history at 72aec54), and pairing_driver.require_approval() refuses while this file exists.

why.claim: The decisive comparison is fixed by an exact identity, so the test is not informative.
why.detail: For Palace's own distributed-sheet port, N = 1 and sum over all modes of p/lambda = L C'_h, where C'_h is the static Dirichlet capacitance with the port-face potential also held linear along the port direction. Hence S_h = (1 + delta_h) * H_h(all modes) exactly, with delta_h = C'_h/C_h - 1 >= 0 a STATIC quantity. The out-of-band part of the band sum is at most S_h(1 - N_B)/f_max^2, about 2e-5 relative on L2. So once g >= 1.05 the test's 'co-movement' and its delta were determined by statics: SUPPORTS would have been close to predetermined, and three consequential Palace solves would have confirmed an identity.
why.verification: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. Derivation re-done; my own implementation (spectral.port_constrained_energy) reproduces the dense-eigen sheet delta to 1.1e-12 (n = 3) and 1.2e-12 (n = 4) on synthetic slabs (identities.json). Found by the math reviewer.

why.claim: Palace's saved refined mesh has a 'nodes' section, which read_mfem_mesh refuses: the attempt would have failed at level 1 after two Palace solves.
why.verification: VERIFIED from source and records: pinned geodata.cpp:1554-1570 calls EnsureNodes() unless Model.RemoveCurvature is set (not set); every committed log prints 'Mesh curvature order: 1'. The reviewers also reproduced the saved format with a pinned-tree build. The driver's test and mock encoded the wrong assumption.

why.claim: The nesting predicate (every new vertex is a previous-level edge midpoint) rejects MFEM's genuinely nested level 1 -> 2 bisection, so the record would have been UNQUALIFIED.
why.verification: CONFIRMED BY REVIEWER EMULATION (MFEM c444b17 built from source in the reviewers' scratch space), and consistent with bisection closure, which splits edges created within the same refinement pass. Not re-run by me. A correct check would locate each fine vertex in a coarse element (barycentric prolongation) before the Galerkin identity.

why.claim: Integrity required exactly 6 modes, but Palace writes every converged eigenpair.
why.verification: VERIFIED from committed records: N2R's config has Eigenmode N = 6 and its eig.csv has 9 rows.

why.claim: The refinement box omits the ground edge on three sides: the island-to-ground gap is 0.040 mm on x-, y- and y+ and 0.020 mm only on x+, so 'the whole 0.020 mm gap' was wrong.
why.verification: VERIFIED from the mesh: median gaps 0.0400 (x-), 0.0200 (x+), 0.0400 (y-), 0.0400 (y+) mm. My error: I took the minimum distance as if it held on every side.

why.claim: A workflow_dispatch workflow must exist on the default branch to be dispatched; the approval procedure omitted that separately approvable merge.
why.verification: VERIFIED: origin/main has no static-band-pairing.yml; commit 30fca75 records the rule, which is why first-moment-n2r.yml was merged to main in PR #9.
